items.title: command-catalog-smoke asserts bidirectional dispatch/registry consistency and exits 0
items.context: In packages/main/src/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.ts, replace the full-registry loop (currently ~lines 152-166) so it branches on whether entry.canonicalName is in AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES. Dispatchable entries: every example field schema-valid AND validateAgentDispatchRequest returns the entry. Retired entries (e.g. lattice-review-channel): dispatch agentType schema rejects the canonicalName AND validateAgentDispatchRequest throws. Verify: node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js exits 0.

happy.desc: Run node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js -> exits 0 with stdout matching /command catalog smoke passed: \d+ commands/; WHY: proves the bidirectional consistency guard passes on clean main after the fix

Inspect source: for every AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY entry whose canonicalName IS in AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES, the loop asserts schemaAccepts(dispatch, agentType, entry.canonicalName) === true AND validateAgentDispatchRequest({...example, phase}) returns the entry; WHY: forward direction — dispatchable entries pass schema + runtime contract

Inspect source: for every AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY entry whose canonicalName is NOT in AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES, the loop asserts schemaAccepts(dispatch, agentType, entry.canonicalName) === false AND validateAgentDispatchRequest throws with message matching /retired|unknown/; WHY: reverse direction — retired entries (lattice-review-channel) actively rejected by both schema and runtime

edge.desc: The branch condition uses AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES.includes(entry.canonicalName) (or equivalent Set lookup), not a hardcoded name like lattice-review-channel; WHY: any future retired entry automatically covered by the guard without code changes

The existing dispatchable-entry assertions (schema-valid example fields + validateAgentDispatchRequest returns entry) are structurally preserved from the original loop, not weakened; WHY: forward-direction coverage must not regress while adding reverse direction

The success message still reports MAIN_TOOLS.length (command count), not AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY.length; WHY: existing output contract preserved — the smoke tests the catalog, count reflects commands not registry entries

adversarial.desc: Mutation test: if AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES were changed to include lattice-review-channel (removing the filter on line 314 of agent-dispatch-registry.ts), the smoke must fail because the retired-branch assertions (schema rejects + throws /retired|unknown/) would fire on an entry that now passes schema validation; WHY: the guard is un-gameable — widening the accepted set triggers the reverse assertion

Mutation test: if the retired-entry assertion block were deleted entirely (keeping only dispatchable-entry assertions), the smoke would silently skip retired entries without verifying rejection; the fix must actively assert rejection, not just omit retired entries from the positive-path loop; WHY: bidirectional contract requires both directions — skip is not proof of rejection

validateAgentDispatchRequest must throw (not return a falsy/null value) for retired types, and the smoke must use assert.throws with a regex matching /retired|unknown/ on the error message; WHY: fail-closed contract — a silent null return would let a retired agent pass the guard without detection

items.title: command-catalog-smoke registered in validate.commands normal tier
items.context: Add node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js to lattice.config.json validate.commands (NOT the fast focus set; it spawns real CLI subprocesses and compares help output). The build step already runs first in validate, so no new build dependency is introduced.

happy.desc: lattice.config.json validate.commands contains an entry for node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js (either as a plain string or as an object with command/args pointing to it); WHY: proves the smoke is registered in the validation pipeline
The entry does NOT have focus: ["fast"] (or any focus property); WHY: the smoke spawns real CLI subprocesses and compares help output, so it belongs on the normal tier, not the fast focus set

edge.desc: The command-catalog-smoke entry appears after the build step (npm run build or equivalent) in the validate.commands array; WHY: the smoke imports from dist/ so it depends on a fresh build — ordering must satisfy this dependency
The entry format is consistent with other normal-tier entries in validate.commands (string or {command,args} without focus); WHY: config consistency — avoids silent parse-skip by the validate runner

adversarial.desc: Run node packages/main/dist/cli.js validate --story=B-3783 and confirm command-catalog-smoke.js appears in the execution output (not silently skipped); WHY: wiring must be reached by lattice validate — a malformed or unreachable config entry would make the guard toothless

If the entry were removed from validate.commands, lattice validate would no longer exercise the bidirectional consistency guard; verify the entry is present and not duplicated; WHY: single-point enforcement — the smoke is only useful if validate runs it
